summary: Iteration 009 adds facial affect analysis to Bay-Max with valence/arousal dimensional modeling, EMA smoothing, confidence-gated strategy bias, and strict clinical language safety. MediaPipe Face Landmarker serves as the primary backend (py-feat incompatible with Python 3.11), with NullEmotionAnalyzer always available as fallback. Smoothed affect state influences response strategy and tone without overriding safety or critical interactions. Session-level affect summaries are written to memory only when stable (≥30sec) and confident (≥0.65), with clinical language blocklist enforcement. Comprehensive artifact logging provides timeline data, strategy changes, and verification manifests. All 386 automated tests pass (356 existing + 30 new). Manual affect verification requires test images not available on headless Sol.

known_issues: py-feat backend blocked by setuptools/pkg_resources incompatibility with Python 3.11 — interface exists for future integration
MediaPipe Face Landmarker blendshape-to-affect mapping uses custom heuristics — not clinically validated for emotion recognition
VT930-VT936 manual affect verification tests not_run on Sol — requires local laptop with test images for replay testing
Affect analysis requires good lighting and front-facing poses for reliable confidence scores from MediaPipe
MediaPipe Face Landmarker model auto-downloads on first use (~10MB) — cached after initial run
Clinical language safety relies on substring matching — may miss paraphrased clinical terms in edge cases
Session-level affect summaries have lower salience (0.4) — may be less prominent in memory retrieval than other episodic memories
deviations_from_prompt: py-feat backend not implemented due to Python 3.11 incompatibility — MediaPipe used as primary real backend instead
MediaPipe Face Landmarker used instead of py-feat Action Units — blendshape coefficients mapped to valence/arousal
Manual verification tests (VT930-VT936) marked not_run rather than executed — Sol has no camera and test images not provided
Affect artifact logging implemented as separate module (affect_artifacts.py) rather than integrated into existing artifact system
EmotionResult schema uses dimensional valence/arousal model rather than discrete emotion labels for richer affect representation
risks: MediaPipe blendshape-to-affect mapping not validated against ground truth emotion datasets — may misinterpret cultural or individual expression variations
Affect analysis adds computational overhead — MediaPipe Face Landmarker ~50-100ms per frame on CPU may impact real-time performance
Clinical language safety depends on comprehensive blocklist maintenance — new clinical terms may emerge that aren't blocked
Memory consolidation with affect summaries could create persistent bias if affect analysis is systematically wrong for certain users
Low confidence thresholds (0.6) may still allow some incorrect affect interpretations to influence system behavior

Should affect timelines be accessible to users for self-reflection, or kept internal for privacy?
How should cultural differences in emotional expression be handled in a production deployment?
